implementation_notes: JSR-385 (the successor of JSR-363, still Java 8+) standardises the pattern as interfaces: Quantity<Q extends Quantity<Q>>, Unit<Q>, UnitConverter and the per-dimension quantity types such as Length, Mass and Temperature, with Indriya as the reference implementation - Quantities.getQuantity(3, KILO(METRE)).add(...).to(METRE) is the whole arithmetic. The specification answers the affine-unit question for you: operations execute as if the operands were converted to system units, so 2 degC + 2 K equals 275.15 K + 2 K and 2 degC + 1 degC is 274.15 degC rather than 3 degC. New units and prefixes are data in the system of units rather than code, and the API is separated from the implementation by design, so the same client code can run on another JSR-385 implementation.
pitfalls: Nothing here is a compile-time check: dimension errors surface as UnconvertibleException or IncommensurableException at run time, so the unit tests carry the burden that F# units of measure would put on the compiler.
Equality of BigDecimal-backed quantities includes scale, so 1.0 m and 1.00 m can be unequal unless the implementation normalises; rely on compareTo for ordering.
The API and one implementation must be wired consistently - again, mixing two providers or two unit systems in one JVM yields unit instances that are not equal.

variants.name: Java 17 record over a unit enum
variants.implementation_notes: If a full JSR-385 stack is unacceptable, a Java 17 record gives the value semantics for free - the compiler generates the accessors, equals, hashCode and toString from the components (see the Java language guide on record classes) - and one static Map holds the factors to the dimension's base unit. Use the compact constructor to validate and normalise to a canonical unit so that raw amounts can never be attached and 1 km and 1000 m collapse to one value; the record is immutable by construction, so the only way to change it is to build a new one.
pitfalls: Records give component-based equality, so without normalisation in the compact constructor 1 km and 1000 m are different values with different hash codes.
Chained conversions in binary floating point drift; use BigDecimal or a scaled long when conversions must round-trip exactly.
A record is still only as good as its unit enum: a String unit component would make the value data-driven but reintroduce the free-text unit anti-pattern.
